The Fellowship of His Sufferings
FEL-low-ship
noun phrase
From the Greek koinonia, “fellowship” or “sharing,” joined to pathema, “suffering,” in Paul’s desire to share the sufferings of Christ.

Biblical Definition

The fellowship of His sufferings is that communion with Christ in affliction by which the believer is conformed to his crucified Lord, and so made partaker also of His resurrection life. Paul, having counted all things but loss for the excellency of the knowledge of Christ Jesus his Lord, breathed out this great longing: That I may know him, and the power of his resurrection, and the fellowship of his sufferings, being made conformable unto his death (Phil 3:10). The dictionary marks this phrase as the heart of the Christian’s union with Christ: to know Christ is not only to be saved by His sufferings, but to be joined to Him in them, to fill up that which is behind of the afflictions of Christ in the flesh, for His body’s sake, which is the church (Col 1:24). So the Scripture teaches that if we suffer with Him, we shall also be glorified together (Rom 8:17); for the order is fixed, the cross before the crown, the death before the rising. The believer does not earn his salvation by suffering, for the atonement was finished upon the cross; but being united to Christ by faith, he is made like Him, sharing the reproach, the loss, and the affliction of his Master in this present age. And this fellowship is no mere sorrow, for it is fellowship, communion with a living Christ who suffered and now reigns; and the soul that shares His sufferings shall surely share His glory.

Webster 1828 Definition

The believer’s communion with Christ in affliction, by which he is conformed to his Lord and partakes of His resurrection.

expand to see more

THE FELLOWSHIP OF HIS SUFFERINGS, communion with Christ in affliction, conforming the believer to his Lord.

Paul counted all things loss that he might know Christ and this fellowship.

To suffer with Christ is to be made conformable unto His death.

If we suffer with Him, we shall also be glorified together.

The order is fixed: the cross before the crown, the death before the rising.

Key Scripture

Phil 3:10 — "That I may know him, and the power of his resurrection, and the fellowship of his sufferings, being made conformable unto his death;"

Rom 8:17 — "And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together."

Col 1:24 — "Who now rejoice in my sufferings for you, and fill up that which is behind of the afflictions of Christ in my flesh for his body’s sake, which is the church:"

2Co 1:5 — "For as the sufferings of Christ abound in us, so our consolation also aboundeth by Christ."

Modern Corruption

A treasure of Scripture; the believer’s union with his crucified Lord in suffering, which goes before the sharing of His glory.

expand to see more

The fellowship of His sufferings has drawn little redefinition from the present age, surviving as a phrase of deep comfort to the afflicted saint. The dictionary records it that the reader may mark the union with Christ that joins the believer to his Lord in suffering as truly as in glory.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that union with Christ means conformity to His death before participation in His glory. The believer is not saved by his sufferings, for the atonement was finished upon the cross; yet being joined to Christ by faith, he is made like Him, bearing the reproach and affliction of his Master in this present age. If we suffer with Him, we shall also be glorified together; the cross goes before the crown. Let the suffering saint know that his afflictions are not a sign of God’s desertion but the very mark of his fellowship with a living and reigning Christ.

Hebrew Roots

From the Greek for “fellowship in suffering,” the phrase names communion with Christ in His afflictions.

expand to see more

The Fellowship of His Sufferings — Greek koinonia ton pathematon, “sharing in the sufferings.”

It is communion with Christ in affliction, not a price paid for salvation.

By it the believer is made conformable unto Christ’s death.

Paul desired it above all earthly gain, counting all things loss.

It goes before the sharing of Christ’s resurrection and glory.

Usage

"To know Christ is to be joined to Him in His sufferings as well as His glory."

"If we suffer with Him, we shall also be glorified together."

"The afflictions of the saint are the very mark of his fellowship with his Lord."
